log.reply:
# Proposal: Guided AI GRC Build for Tamarack Instruments

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel (stated as budget holder)
**Program:** Guided AI GRC Build, AI Governance Academy
**Basis:** Discovery call notes of 6 October 2026, with Dana Whitfield, Ravi Okafor and Ingrid Solberg

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. It has about 1,100 staff and reported revenue described on the discovery call as "in the US$200 to 300 million range." That band was given verbally and has not been checked against filings.

The Client's AI footprint is at an early stage:

- **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
- **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
- **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

An internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded that no inventory of AI systems exists. The regulatory drivers are the EU AI Act and GDPR. ISO/IEC 42001 is a certification target, with work to start next year. The start date is not fixed.

Your stated objective is: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."

Three constraints shape the build:

- The approved budget is up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
- Customer data must stay in the EU.
- The German works council must be consulted before anything touches production staff.

A decision is expected by 15 December 2026.

## 2. Why a Guided Build Rather Than Pure Consulting Delivery

In a conventional consulting engagement, a consultant writes the governance documents and hands them over. The Client receives artifacts but often lacks the people who know how to run them. The Guided AI GRC Build reverses that model:

- Your own build team produces every artifact during weekly workshops, coaching sessions and structured asynchronous work.
- Our role is to supply method, templates, challenge and review.
- At the end of twelve weeks, your team has built the system, retains it and can operate it without us.

This model fits Tamarack Instruments for three reasons:

1. **Incumbent systems.** The Client already runs an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS, an ISO 9001 quality management system and an internal audit function. Each new AI governance process should attach to these structures rather than sit beside them. That integration can only be done well by the people who run them.
2. **Lasting knowledge.** The two internal auditors on the build team gain working knowledge of the AIMS they will later review. The Client should decide how to preserve audit independence for any later assurance work.
3. **Relevant expertise.** Works council consultation and the EU data residency constraint call for local knowledge that our consultants do not hold.

The program applies three principles throughout: Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human.

It draws on two working frameworks:

- GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook)
- Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen)

Board-layer material comes from AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards).

## 3. The Twelve-Week Spine, Tailored to Tamarack Instruments

### 3.1 Inventory priority

The inventory in Week 2 enters systems in the following order. Systems not named in the discovery notes are Unknown and will be surfaced during Week 2.

1. **Customer service chatbot.** It is the only system stated as deployed, so it carries live exposure today. Its hosting location and data flows are Unknown. They must be recorded against the EU data residency constraint.
2. **AI visual inspection pilot.** Your stated objective ties governance to its move into production in Q2 2027. Whether it touches production staff is Unknown. The answer determines when works council consultation is triggered.
3. **AI sales forecasting.** It is planned for next year and enters as a planned system. Governance can then be applied before procurement or build begins.

### 3.2 Readiness mapping and integration points

**ISO/IEC 42001.** The table below maps each week's artifacts to ISO/IEC 42001 readiness themes. This mapping supports readiness only. It is not a promise of certification or of any audit outcome.

**Incumbent frameworks.** The Profile Block names the ISMS, the QMS and the internal audit function. It does not identify any specific register, procedure or record within them. Integration points are therefore shown as Unknown until mobilization confirms which artifacts exist. The one named attachment point is the June 2026 internal audit finding.

### 3.3 Week-by-week plan

| Week | Spine focus | Tailoring for Tamarack Instruments | ISO/IEC 42001 readiness theme | Integration point |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| W1 | Mobilization, charter and roles | Charter scope across the Netherlands, Germany and the United States; executive steering checkpoint | Context of the organization; leadership | Unknown |
| W2 | AI system inventory | Chatbot, visual inspection pilot and sales forecasting entered in the priority order above; discovery of other systems | Context; AI system scope | June 2026 internal audit finding (no inventory of AI systems) |
| W3 | Classification and risk methodology | EU AI Act classification approach for each inventoried system (confirm with external counsel) | Planning; risk criteria | Unknown |
| W4 | Risk and impact assessments | Impact assessments for the chatbot and visual inspection pilot; GDPR considerations (confirm with external counsel) | AI risk assessment; AI system impact assessment | Unknown |
| W5 | Risk register and treatment | Treatment plans for the first two systems; data residency treatment for the chatbot | Risk treatment | Unknown |
| W6 | Policy set and mid-point steering | Core AI policy set drafted for adoption; mid-point steering checkpoint | Leadership; AI policy | Unknown |
| W7 | Operating procedures and lifecycle governance | Lifecycle gates covering the move from pilot to production for visual inspection | Operation; AI system life cycle | Unknown |
| W8 | Vendor and supplier governance; evidence collection begins | Supplier review for any third-party AI components (suppliers Unknown); evidence collection starts | Third-party relationships; documented information | Unknown |
| W9 | Governed workflows and human oversight (Slow AI Kitchen) | Human oversight design for at least two workflows; works council consultation need assessed for any workflow touching production staff | Operation; human oversight | Unknown |
| W10 | Testing, evaluation and monitoring | Performance and monitoring criteria for chatbot and inspection outputs | Performance evaluation; monitoring | Unknown |
| W11 | Incident response, change management and evidence review | AI incident and change routes defined; first evidence review | Improvement; nonconformity and corrective action | Unknown |
| W12 | Audit readiness review, evidence walkthrough and closing steering | Walkthrough with the internal auditors on the build team; closing steering checkpoint | Internal audit readiness; management review readiness | June 2026 internal audit finding (closure evidence for review) |

## 4. Contracted Outcome: Minimum Viable AIMS at Week 12

The program contracts for a minimum viable AIMS at Week 12, defined as follows:

1. An adopted charter.
2. A populated inventory.
3. An operating risk register.
4. An adopted core policy set.
5. At least two governed AI workflows in production use.
6. Evidence collection running for at least four weeks.

**Delivery risk on element 5.** The chatbot is the only system currently stated as deployed. The visual inspection pilot is targeted for production in Q2 2027, and whether that falls before Week 12 depends on a start date that is Unknown. The second qualifying workflow is therefore Unknown. It must be identified by Week 2 and confirmed at the Week 1 or Week 6 steering checkpoint.

**Policy adoption.** Adoption of the charter and policies may carry legal effect for employees and works council matters. Confirm with external counsel.

## 5. Client Team Commitment

The figures below are estimates of hours per person per week. They cover the workshop, coaching and asynchronous work, and they are not actuals. Peak weeks are also estimates.

| Role | Estimated hours per week | Estimated peak weeks |
|---|---|---|
| General Counsel | 3 to 4 | W1, W3, W6, W12 |
| CISO | 4 to 5 | W2, W5, W8, W11 |
| Head of Quality | 4 to 5 | W7, W10, W11 |
| Head of Data | 5 to 6 | W2, W4, W9, W10 |
| German plant manager | 3 to 4 | W2, W4, W9 |
| Internal auditor (each of two) | 3 to 4 | W2, W8, W11, W12 |

Executive steering checkpoints in Weeks 1, 6 and 12 add an estimated 1.5 hours per attendee. Steering membership is Unknown and will be confirmed at mobilization.

## 6. Steering Cadence

| Checkpoint | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Week 1 | Confirm scope, team, risks to delivery and the second workflow candidate. |
| Week 6 | Review spine status, the artifact register and blockers, and take any scope decisions. Works council consultation timing, if triggered, is reviewed here. |
| Week 12 | Attest the minimum viable AIMS against the six-element definition. Review the evidence sample index and the 12-month operating plan. |

## 7. Logistics and Price

**Format.** One live virtual workshop, one coaching session and structured asynchronous implementation each week, for 12 weeks. The following are Unknown and will be agreed at contracting:

- Start date
- Session times across operating time zones
- Working language
- Hosting arrangements for Client artifacts

Artifact storage should respect the constraint that customer data stays in the EU.

**Price.** US$60,000 for the full program. The Profile Block states budget approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year. Whether the program start date falls within that fiscal year is Unknown. Payment schedule and contract terms are to be agreed. Confirm with external counsel.

## 8. Next Step

A decision is expected by 15 December 2026. We propose a 45-minute confirmation session before that date, with the following agenda:

1. Confirm the start date relative to the Q2 2027 visual inspection objective.
2. Identify which ISMS, QMS and internal audit artifacts exist, so integration points can replace the Unknown entries above.
3. Confirm the second governed workflow candidate.
4. Agree steering membership.

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.

elements.evidence: Section 2: "The two internal auditors on the build team gain working knowledge of the AIMS they will later review." The Profile Block states only that an internal audit function exists and that two internal auditors are in AUDIENCE_ROLES. It does not say the internal audit function will review the AIMS.

fail_indicators_seen: A fact about the Client that the input does not contain is presented as fact (an incumbent function relation: the internal auditors "will later review" the AIMS)
judgment_calls: The "will later review" sentence is the main basis for FAIL. I read it as an asserted attribution about the incumbent internal audit function, which v1.14.3 guidance treats as a failure. Another scorer could read it as proposed or conditional work and pass it, especially since the next sentence says the Client should decide how to preserve audit independence.

The W12 integration entry "June 2026 internal audit finding (closure evidence for review)" implies the finding is open and will be closed. The Block does not state the finding's status. I treated this as borderline and did not rely on it.
The phrase "That integration can only be done well by the people who run them" implies the Client's staff operate the ISMS and QMS. I treated it as mild and did not rely on it.
I scored item 4 as not applicable because Mode A has no weekly assignments. Another scorer could apply it to the week-by-week table, but that would not change the verdict.
I accepted the W2 and W12 integration entries that name the June 2026 audit finding as attaching to an artifact the Block states.
score.reasoning: The structural checklist items are met: one mode, spine and steering intact, constants unaltered, evidence collection at W8, closing line present. Items 4 and 5 are not applicable to Mode A. The proposal is otherwise careful, rendering unknowns as Unknown and labelling effort figures as estimates. It still states in Section 2 that the internal auditors "will later review" the AIMS. That is an incumbent-function relation the Profile Block does not contain, so a fail indicator is present. Under the strict rule that partial compliance is FAIL, the verdict is FAIL.
